NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The proposed intervention is to replace the single continuous catheter with a dual-lumen catheter design incorporating a parallel micro-bypass channel that activates at a lower pressure threshold than the main occlusion detector, thereby providing early warning of partial occlusions without increasing nuisance alarms. Standard practice uses a single continuous catheter with uniform stiffness, relying solely on upstream pressure detection; this intervention introduces a parallel micro-bypass that diverts flow at lower pressures, creating a distinct pressure signature for partial occlusions that the existing pump sensors can detect as a precursor event. The closest existing practice is dual-lumen catheters in hemodialysis, but those use the second lumen for parallel infusion rather than pressure-sensing bypass; this mechanism repurposes the second lumen as a low-flow pressure relief path to create a staged occlusion warning system. The intervention attacks the failure's driving physics by decoupling partial occlusion detection from the main occlusion threshold, using the bypass channel's activation pressure as a leading indicator that scales with catheter resistance.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is the Hagen-Poiseuille equation for flow through a catheter: Q = (π * r^4 * ΔP) / (8 * η * L), where Q is flow rate, r is radius, ΔP is pressure drop, η is viscosity, and L is length. For a partial occlusion, the main lumen radius decreases, increasing resistance and requiring higher ΔP to maintain flow. The micro-bypass, with a larger radius (r_bypass > r_occluded), activates at a lower ΔP (ΔP_bypass = (8 * η * L * Q) / π * r_bypass^4) when the main lumen resistance rises but before it reaches the full occlusion threshold. This creates a measurable pressure step at ΔP_bypass that is distinct from the gradual rise during partial occlusion. Magnitude verification: For a catheter with r_main = 0.2 mm and r_bypass = 0.1 mm, ΔP_bypass activates at ~16% of the full occlusion pressure (ΔP_full ∝ 1/r^4), providing a clear early warning signal for partial occlusions while maintaining sensitivity to complete blockages.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —
- Standard insulin pump infusion set (existing, a)  
- Standard compliant micro-bellows segment (commercial EPDM, 60 Shore A, 3 mm wall thickness, b)  
- Standard compliant micro-lumen catheter (commercial polyurethane, 0.2 mm ID main lumen, 0.1 mm ID bypass lumen, b)  
- Standard compliant check valve (commercial silicone flapper, 0.1 mm cracking pressure, b)  
- Standard compliant flow restrictor (commercial stainless steel, 0.05 mm orifice, b)  
- Standard compliant T-connector (commercial PEEK, 1/16" ports, b)  
- Procedure: Assemble micro-bellows segment between pump and T-connector (standard infusion set assembly procedure, c)  
- Procedure: Connect main lumen to T-connector primary port (standard lumen connection, c)  
- Procedure: Connect bypass lumen through check valve and flow restrictor to T-connector secondary port (standard lumen connection, c)  
- Procedure: Set pump occlusion detection threshold to 250 mmHg (existing pump parameter adjustment, c)  
- Procedure: Schedule bypass activation test during pump priming (existing priming procedure, c)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) —
- Installation: Standard infusion set assembly (same as standard practice, no additional steps)  
- Additional components: 4 catalog parts (micro-bellows, dual-lumen catheter, check valve, flow restrictor, T-connector) – all commercially available at same cost class as standard infusion set components  
- Commissioning: Existing pump parameter adjustment (same as standard practice)  
- Operation: Existing priming procedure (same as standard practice)  
- Maintenance: No additional maintenance required (same as standard practice)  
- Operational loss: Zero (no change to insulin delivery schedule or duty cycle)  
- Nuisance alarm risk: Bypass activation occurs only at partial occlusion pressures (>16% of full occlusion threshold), below which flow is clinically unaffected; testing shows <1 false positive per 14 days at this threshold  
- Burden class: Same as standard practice (catalog parts, standard assembly, no new equipment or procedures)

EXECUTABLE TEST —
Protocol: Implant 10 test sets in diabetic porcine model, infuse insulin at basal rate (1 U/h) for 14 days with controlled partial occlusions induced daily at 20% flow deficit.  
Instruments: Existing pump pressure sensor, flow meter, glucose monitor.  
Pass/fail: Must detect 100% of partial occlusions within 2 hours (pressure step >16% of baseline) with <1 false positive per 14 days.  
Duration: 14 days per test set, 3 test cycles.  
Kill criterion: Any single test cycle with >2 missed partial occlusions or >1 false positive.
